historical_references.reference: Callista was a Christian martyr and virgin venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. She was the daughter of a Roman senator and was married to a pagan named Publius. She was converted to Christianity by Pope Fabian while in Rome. When Publius discovered her new faith, he attempted to force her to renounce her beliefs. Callista refused and was sent to the mines in Sardinia as punishment. She is said to have suffered martyrdom by being beheaded in Sardinia.

Callista, also known as St. Callixtus, was a Christian martyr and saint. She was a Roman slave and was martyred during the reign of Emperor Hadrian in the 2nd century AD in Rome. According to legend, she was a deaf-mute who converted several members of her household to Christianity. When her master discovered her new faith, he had her tortured and then executed by being beheaded.
